<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via getMetaItemCached (symbol, a method of class ProtocolSearchAndCacheFacet))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d0c377beb988b990e77aa4763fd5e4b429d8de4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `da3ef679fbcdaf369f0f08285eb49f5ecdd14f42` — the merge of head `7ff2b9e528edafe5baf30284f84939be5127e926` into base `0d0c377beb988b990e77aa4763fd5e4b429d8de4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin da3ef679fbcdaf369f0f08285eb49f5ecdd14f42 && git checkout da3ef679fbcdaf369f0f08285eb49f5ecdd14f42
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0d0c377beb988b990e77aa4763fd5e4b429d8de4 7ff2b9e528edafe5baf30284f84939be5127e926 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0d0c377beb988b990e77aa4763fd5e4b429d8de4 && git merge --no-ff 7ff2b9e528edafe5baf30284f84939be5127e926

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0d0c377beb988b990e77aa4763fd5e4b429d8de4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0d0c377beb988b990e77aa4763fd5e4b429d8de4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

domain:server#5 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5o8PE7ZtVjcor51wBZ

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:元数据按名读取的缓存出口(默认的 `GET /api/v1/meta/:type/:name`)里,`Last-Modified` 不再填「这次读取的时间」。条目来自 `sys_metadata` 存储行时,填该行的 `updated_at`(最近一次保存或发布的时间);条目来自代码或文件、平台不知道它何时改过时,不发这个头。
- 为什么改:同一条没改过的元数据,两次读到的 `Last-Modified` 不一样而 ETag 相同,这个头在说假话,还让 #31171 的测试在合并队列里抖过两次。
- 风险与回滚:只改头的取值;ETag、`Cache-Control: private, no-cache`、`If-None-Match` 的 304 全部不变,按名读取的响应信封逐字节不变(时间走进程内不可序列化的符号,不进 JSON)。回滚即 revert。
- 先看:`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.ts`(采用存储行处记下 `updated_at`,返回信封时挂上);`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-search-and-cache.ts`(`lastModified` 改读它,没有就不给键);新文件 `served-row-changed-at.ts`。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol exec vitest run src/protocol.cached-item-last-modified.test.ts`,预期 4 个用例全过:两次读同一个时间、保存和发布各自推进它、代码条目没有 `lastModified` 键。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

席位意见:接受。`Last-Modified` 现在取条目所服务的存储行的 `updated_at`,代码随包发布的条目不发这个头;只改元数据协议这一层,REST 入口不动,新鲜度仍只由 ETag 决定。

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · `domain:server#5` · Head-sha `7ff2b9e528edafe5baf30284f84939be5127e926` · 2026-11-07T20:09Z

- **Shape:** 8 files, +431/−4, read from the diff. `readMetaItem` records the adopted `sys_metadata` row's `updated_at` (else `created_at`, through the repository's own `canonicalIsoInstant`, now exported) on its envelope as a non-enumerable `Symbol.for` property (`served-row-changed-at.ts`); `getMetaItemCached` answers it, or no `lastModified` key. Draft reads and items no stored row serves carry none. The symbol never serialises, so `GetMetaItemResponseSchema` answers and every REST/MCP pin are unchanged; a spread copy loses it, which omits the header (the safe direction). `meta-item-read-routes.ts` untouched.
- **Premise measured:** on main the cached read set `lastModified: new Date().toISOString()`; the dev's ablation (read time put back) reds 3, CONTROL green.
- **Pins:** two reads of one unchanged stored item answer the same `Last-Modified`; a save moves it; a code-shipped item answers no header; ETag / `Cache-Control: no-cache` unchanged (REST-level test in `packages/rest`).
- **Gates:** head check-runs 35 `success`, 13 skipped, none red or pending. `check-expected-skips`: OK, all 13 in main's roster (exit 0). No governed path, 435 changed lines ≤ 3000. The dev's `dispatch-gates --commands`: 69 derived, 69 run, all exit 0. Mergeable state `clean`.
- **Accepted deviations:** surface beyond the claim (`protocol-meta-item-reads.ts`, new `served-row-changed-at.ts`, the one-word export in `sys-metadata-repository.ts`, the engine-double ledger rows from its gate's own `--write`): the change time is reachable only inside `readMetaItem`. `origin/main` merged once at `66bf5b4a`; main has moved since, touching none of these files, and the queue builds on current main.
- **Out of scope:** the `CLOCK_HEADERS` comment in runtime's `mcp-object-schema-mask.test.ts` (#31195) now overstates for `Last-Modified`: a comment-only follow-up, carried by this seat. `Clause-②: no` (the field is already optional in the published `http-cache.zod.ts`), `Metadata-protocol: none`, `Skills-docs:` n/a. Changeset patch.
- **Landing:** ungoverned. `Fixes #31196`. Ready + auto-merge.
